title: The Concept of Social Capital
text:
Social capital refers to the resources inherent within social relationships, networks, and community structures. It represents the value derived from sustained connections—such as trust, reciprocity, and mutual obligation—which can facilitate collective action and influence individual outcomes.

Research suggests that strong local social ties can significantly improve economic resilience and public health outcomes by creating informal support systems. For instance, well-connected neighborhoods often exhibit lower rates of crime because the shared norms and surveillance function act as a deterrent to antisocial behavior.

Furthermore, institutional analysis shows that formal organizations benefit greatly when they can tap into existing levels of trust within their operational environment. High social capital acts as an intangible lubricant for governance, making cooperation across diverse groups more efficient.
